message.content: {"schema_version":"teaching-unit.v0.4.0","input_manifest_sha256":"e8df7edddacd3640adb97c6b61e40d79dc158f955e73c174601cbbb699eb3379","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mt-class-d:lineage:110","source_registry_sha256":"35425fc1b75886d4bce9129f5de9443ae8cee634cff4a62363bbcd7cc017fe32","units":[{"unit_id":"sec07-u01","module_id":"sec07-m01","objective_ids":["sec07-F01-understand","sec07-F02-understand","sec07-F03-understand","sec07-F04-understand","sec07-F05-understand","sec07-F06-understand","sec07-F07-understand","sec07-F08-understand","sec07-F09-understand","sec07-F10-understand","sec07-F11-understand","sec07-F12-understand","sec07-F13-understand","sec07-F14-understand","sec07-F15-understand","sec07-F16-understand","sec07-F17-understand","sec07-F18-understand","sec07-F19-understand","sec07-F20-understand","sec07-F21-understand","sec07-F22-understand","sec07-F23-understand","sec07-F24-understand","sec07-R10-understand","sec07-R11-understand","sec07-R16-understand"],"title":{"text":"General driving and turns","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F02","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F05","sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-F11","sec07-F12","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-F15","sec07-F16","sec07-F17","sec07-F18","sec07-F19","sec07-F20","sec07-F21","sec07-F22","sec07-F23","sec07-F24","sec07-R10","sec07-R11","sec07-R16"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Courtesy, suitable speed and a safe clear movement belong together. Expecting another driver to compensate does not establish a safe gap.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]},{"text":"A missed location does not justify stopping or reversing in the travel lane. The source separately calls for a walk-around before reversing a parked car.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02"]},{"text":"The obedience instruction names several sources of traffic control. Personal preference is not an exception to following them.","fact_ids":["sec07-F03"]},{"text":"The source gives different advance distances for town and rural turns, with the rural distance longer. The context belongs with the signaling instruction.","fact_ids":["sec07-F04"]},{"text":"The basic keep-right advice has the stated entering-traffic context. It does not create unrestricted use of the leftmost lane or shoulder.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05"]},{"text":"The correction is a later properly prepared turn. A missed opportunity does not remove lane, signal or safety requirements.","fact_ids":["sec07-F06"]},{"text":"The rule retains a direction to use the shoulder. Personal convenience is not that direction.","fact_ids":["sec07-F07"]},{"text":"The posted limit does not promise a suitable speed in bad conditions. Matching conditions can require a lower speed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08"]},{"text":"The listed interstate guidance distinguishes vehicle classes and covers day and night. Keep the vehicle classes and coverage of day and night together when reading the listed schedule.","fact_ids":["sec07-F09"]},{"text":"The urban-area provision groups the listed vehicles together and covers day and night. Keep it separate from the other road schedules.","fact_ids":["sec07-F10"]},{"text":"The listed two-lane schedule distinguishes vehicle classes and daytime from nighttime. Those are the source’s categories, not a permission to choose a limit by convenience.","fact_ids":["sec07-F11"]},{"text":"The allowance is tied to the stated overtaking maneuver and safe return. It is not a general change to every speed limit.","fact_ids":["sec07-F12"]},{"text":"Passing requires a safe opportunity as well as the appropriate road position. A signal does not itself establish room or safety.","fact_ids":["sec07-F13"]},{"text":"The permitted situations do not include leaving the roadway or using the shoulder. Preserve both the circumstance and the roadway limit.","fact_ids":["sec07-F14"]},{"text":"The source connects the side of the turn with the nearest entry and destination lane, rather than an unrestricted sweep across lanes.","fact_ids":["sec07-F15"]},{"text":"A right turn should not be widened by an initial left swing or a far-lane finish. The path is part of safe lane use.","fact_ids":["sec07-F16"]},{"text":"The instruction combines avoiding the approaching traffic path with allowing room for an opposing left turn. These requirements belong together.","fact_ids":["sec07-F17"]},{"text":"The source retains visibility, approaching-traffic and location conditions. Missing a turn does not remove them.","fact_ids":["sec07-F18"]},{"text":"Lane position and safety are separate requirements. Intention or familiarity does not substitute for either.","fact_ids":["sec07-F19"]},{"text":"The general rule concerns a duty to yield and continued crash avoidance. It is not permission to force a claimed priority.","fact_ids":["sec07-F20"]},{"text":"The handbook gives this pedestrian specific protection and says not to use the horn at them. Preserve both parts of the instruction.","fact_ids":["sec07-F21"]},{"text":"The source places duties on both sides. One duty does not cancel the other.","fact_ids":["sec07-F22"]},{"text":"The source combines a sidewalk rule with advice to make a nighttime walker more visible. Visibility advice does not waive the sidewalk rule.","fact_ids":["sec07-F23"]},{"text":"The described walking position faces traffic, and crossing remains subject to the provided crosswalks and applicable laws.","fact_ids":["sec07-F24"]},{"text":"The source distinguishes the usual left-side pass from limited right-side permission. Neither permission authorizes a shoulder pass.","fact_ids":["sec07-R10"]},{"text":"The handbook keeps crash avoidance with yielding rules. A claimed priority is not a reason to force a collision.","fact_ids":["sec07-R11"]},{"text":"Signaling context and lane use remain separate requirements. Match speed to conditions, share the road courteously, and move only when safe and clear of traffic.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Connect rules and actual conditions","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F03"]},"lines":[{"text":"Courtesy does not replace checking whether a movement is safe and clear.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F03"]}],"narration":{"text":"Safe movement combines the traffic rules with the actual conditions. The handbook calls for a suitable speed, courteous sharing and moving only when the path is safe and clear. It also says to obey officers, flaggers, devices and traffic laws. Courtesy is not a substitute for checking a gap, and a favorable signal does not establish that every part of a maneuver is safe. Start with the relevant instruction, then consider the traffic and road conditions rather than assume another road user will compensate for a movement that has not been checked.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F03"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Prepare the later safe turn","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-F04","sec07-F06","sec07-F19","sec07-R16"]},"lines":[{"text":"A missed turn does not remove signaling, lane or safety requirements.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-F04","sec07-F06","sec07-F19","sec07-R16"]},{"text":"A turn needs advance preparation, the proper lane and a safe movement.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-F04","sec07-F06","sec07-F19","sec07-R16"]}],"narration":{"text":"A turn needs advance preparation, the proper lane and a safe movement. The handbook gives different signal lead distances for town and rural roads, with the rural lead longer. If the turn is missed or the signal forgotten, continue to the next intersection and prepare a proper turn there. Do not let a missed opportunity become a reason to cut across traffic. The source separately warns against stopping or reversing in a travel lane and directs the driver toward a safe pull-off. Correcting a route error should preserve the driving rules instead of suspending them.","fact_ids":["sec07-F02","sec07-F04","sec07-F06","sec07-F19","sec07-R16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Keep passing within its conditions","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F07","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-R10"]},"lines":[{"text":"Limited right-side permission does not authorize a shoulder pass.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F07","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-R10"]},{"text":"Passing and shoulder use have their own limits.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F07","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-R10"]}],"narration":{"text":"Passing and shoulder use have their own limits. The handbook describes the usual left-side passing route and permits passing only when safe. Right-side passing is limited to the stated left-turning or wide multi-lane-pavement situations, without leaving the roadway or using the shoulder. The keep-right guidance on several same-direction lanes also includes the entering-traffic context. Keep those rules together without using one as an excuse to bypass another. A slower vehicle or a desired shortcut does not by itself create a safe pass or a direction to drive on the shoulder.","fact_ids":["sec07-F05","sec07-F07","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-R10"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-4","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Identify the relevant speed situation","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-F11","sec07-F12"]},"lines":[{"text":"A listed limit does not promise suitability in every road or weather condition.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-F11","sec07-F12"]},{"text":"The speed material distinguishes road type, vehicle class and, where stated, day from night.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-F11","sec07-F12"]}],"narration":{"text":"The speed material distinguishes road type, vehicle class and, where stated, day from night. The handbook lists separate interstate, urban-area-highway and two-lane schedules rather than one number for every trip. It also says to go below a posted limit when road or weather conditions require it and describes a particular two-lane overtaking allowance tied to returning safely right. Learn the structure without turning any allowance into a general permission to rush. A listed maximum is not a promise that the same speed is suitable for every condition, vehicle or maneuver.","fact_ids":["sec07-F08","sec07-F09","sec07-F10","sec07-F11","sec07-F12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-5","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Keep the path in available space","fact_ids":["sec07-F15","sec07-F16","sec07-F17","sec07-F18","sec07-F19"]},"lines":[{"text":"A signal does not establish that a turn path or turn-around is suitable.","fact_ids":["sec07-F15","sec07-F16","sec07-F17","sec07-F18","sec07-F19"]},{"text":"Turn geometry matters as well as giving a signal.","fact_ids":["sec07-F15","sec07-F16","sec07-F17","sec07-F18","sec07-F19"]}],"narration":{"text":"Turn geometry matters as well as giving a signal. Without special controls, the source describes using the lane nearest the turn’s destination side and entering the nearest lane of the new road. It warns against a right turn that first swings left or finishes wide and against cutting a left turn into approaching traffic. A turn-around has its own clear-view, approaching-traffic and location conditions. Keep the path and the available space in the decision. Intending to turn does not establish room for that path, and missing an earlier turn does not remove the location restrictions.","fact_ids":["sec07-F15","sec07-F16","sec07-F17","sec07-F18","sec07-F19"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-6","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"Do not force a priority claim","fact_ids":["sec07-F20","sec07-F21","sec07-R11"]},"lines":[{"text":"Retain the specific pedestrian protection and the duty to avoid a collision.","fact_ids":["sec07-F20","sec07-F21","sec07-R11"]}],"narration":{"text":"The general yielding principle is not a license to force a claimed priority. The handbook says every driver must still act to avoid striking someone. It gives particular protection to a blind pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane and says not to sound the horn at that person. Keep the specific instruction rather than use a broad slogan to erase it. The useful distinction is between recognizing a duty and trying to seize an advantage. Even when another road user makes an unexpected choice, a priority claim does not make causing a collision the appropriate response.","fact_ids":["sec07-F20","sec07-F21","sec07-R11"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-7","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Check the actual movement","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F22","sec07-F23","sec07-F24"]},"lines":[{"text":"A duty assigned to one road user does not erase another’s duty.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F22","sec07-F23","sec07-F24"]}],"narration":{"text":"A driver sees a pedestrian preparing to cross and assumes courtesy means moving before checking whether the path is clear. What is missing? The handbook combines courtesy with safe, clear movement. It also pairs a driver’s crosswalk yielding duty with the instruction that a pedestrian must not step into a vehicle’s path. Neither duty cancels the other. The walking guidance separately favors sidewalks where they exist, visibility at night and the stated traffic-facing position and crossing places. Recognize the actual road user and situation rather than turn one useful rule into an answer to every movement.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F22","sec07-F23","sec07-F24"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":39,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u01-slide-8","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Keep a permission within its scope","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-F19","sec07-F20","sec07-F21","sec07-F22","sec07-R10","sec07-R11","sec07-R16"]},"lines":[{"text":"A particular allowance does not cancel the other movement conditions.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-F19","sec07-F20","sec07-F21","sec07-F22","sec07-R10","sec07-R11","sec07-R16"]}],"narration":{"text":"For recall, organize the driving decision around control, conditions and movement. Follow the relevant officer, flagger, device or law. Match speed to the road situation rather than treat a posted figure as a universal target. Prepare turns and passes with the required lane, signal, path and safety conditions, and correct missed turns at a later appropriate place. Retain pedestrian duties and the instruction to avoid a collision. This structure helps keep a specific permission, such as a limited passing situation, from being expanded into permission to use a shoulder or force a right-of-way claim.","fact_ids":["sec07-F01","sec07-F03","sec07-F04","sec07-F06","sec07-F07","sec07-F08","sec07-F13","sec07-F14","sec07-F19","sec07-F20","sec07-F21","sec07-F22","sec07-R10","sec07-R11","sec07-R16"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"}]},{"unit_id":"sec07-u02","module_id":"sec07-m02","objective_ids":["sec07-F25-understand","sec07-F26-understand","sec07-F27-understand","sec07-F28-understand","sec07-F29-understand","sec07-F30-understand","sec07-F31-understand","sec07-F32-understand","sec07-F33-understand","sec07-F34-understand","sec07-F35-understand","sec07-R12-understand","sec07-R13-understand"],"title":{"text":"Right of way and school buses","fact_ids":["sec07-F25","sec07-F26","sec07-F27","sec07-F28","sec07-F29","sec07-F30","sec07-F31","sec07-F32","sec07-F33","sec07-F34","sec07-F35","sec07-R12","sec07-R13"]},"why_how":[{"text":"Crossing a sidewalk is distinct from driving along it. The permitted crossing does not remove the duty to yield to pedestrians.","fact_ids":["sec07-F25"]},{"text":"Both examples require the entering or turning vehicle to yield to traffic identified by the source.","fact_ids":["sec07-F26"]},{"text":"The right-side yielding rule works with observation and readiness to brake, rather than replacing those precautions.","fact_ids":["sec07-F27"]},{"text":"Arrival order at the four-way stop does not waive stopping, and entering the main road retains its separate yielding duty.","fact_ids":["sec07-F28"]},{"text":"A favorable opportunity to enter is not enough if the vehicle cannot clear the intersection. A red signal is not an unrestricted turning permission.","fact_ids":["sec07-F30"]},{"text":"The source retains the pedestrian’s position and safety, not merely the fact that the driver has stopped.","fact_ids":["sec07-F31"]},{"text":"Passing the vehicle stopped for a pedestrian is prohibited. The stop should not be treated simply as an obstruction to bypass.","fact_ids":["sec07-F32"]},{"text":"Beginning a pass does not remove the stated yielding duty toward the vehicle being passed.","fact_ids":["sec07-F33"]},{"text":"The instruction combines position, directions and waiting until the emergency vehicle passes. Drivers crossing sidewalks or entering and leaving driveways, alleys and lots yield to pedestrians; sidewalk driving is illegal except to cross.","fact_ids":["sec07-F25"]}},"slides":[{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-slide-1","kind":"opening","title":{"text":"Identify the yielding situation","fact_ids":["sec07-F25","sec07-F26","sec07-F27","sec07-F28"]},"lines":[{"text":"Stopping or signaling does not settle every remaining yielding duty.","fact_ids":["sec07-F25","sec07-F26","sec07-F27","sec07-F28"]}],"narration":{"text":"Yielding duties depend on the place and movement. A driver crossing a sidewalk to or from a driveway, alley or lot yields to pedestrians; that crossing is different from driving along the sidewalk. A left turn yields to oncoming through traffic, and a traffic-circle entrant yields to circulating traffic. Uncontrolled intersections and four-way stops have their own priority arrangements. Identify the situation before borrowing a rule from another one. Having stopped, signaled or begun a maneuver does not establish that every remaining pedestrian or traffic duty has been met.","fact_ids":["sec07-F25","sec07-F26","sec07-F27","sec07-F28"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-slide-2","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"Keep the intersection rules distinct","fact_ids":["sec07-F27","sec07-F28","sec07-F29","sec07-R12"]},"lines":[{"text":"Arrival order does not waive a full stop or the need for room to clear.","fact_ids":["sec07-F27","sec07-F28","sec07-F29","sec07-R12"]},{"text":"An uncontrolled intersection and a four-way stop should not be answered with the same shortcut.","fact_ids":["sec07-F27","sec07-F28","sec07-F29","sec07-R12"]}],"narration":{"text":"An uncontrolled intersection and a four-way stop should not be answered with the same shortcut. The handbook gives the vehicle-on-the-right yielding rule for the uncontrolled intersection and first arrival after a full stop for the four-way stop. It also says a driveway or roadside entrant stops and yields to main-road traffic. Observation and readiness still matter: scan both ways and be prepared to brake, and do not enter an intersection without space to clear it. Recognizing who goes first is not permission to block the crossing or ignore traffic that must be yielded to.","fact_ids":["sec07-F27","sec07-F28","sec07-F29","sec07-R12"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":38,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-slide-3","kind":"concept","title":{"text":"A red-turn permission is conditional","fact_ids":["sec07-F30","sec07-F31","sec07-F32","sec07-R13"]},"lines":[{"text":"A vehicle stopped for a pedestrian is not simply an obstruction to bypass.","fact_ids":["sec07-F30","sec07-F31","sec07-F32","sec07-R13"]},{"text":"A permitted turn on red still has conditions.","fact_ids":["sec07-F30","sec07-F31","sec07-F32","sec07-R13"]}],"narration":{"text":"A permitted turn on red still has conditions. The source requires a stop, the proper lane, a safe turn and attention to any sign prohibiting it; it also describes a left-on-red situation between one-way streets. Pedestrians add a separate consideration: the stated stopped right turn retains the pedestrian-position and safety conditions. A following driver must not pass a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian. Do not let the lead vehicle’s pause become a passing opportunity. The signal color, stopping action and pedestrian protection belong together rather than cancel one another.","fact_ids":["sec07-F30","sec07-F31","sec07-F32","sec07-R13"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":36,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-slide-4","kind":"trap","title":{"text":"A maneuver can still require yielding","fact_ids":["sec07-F29","sec07-F33","sec07-F34"]},"lines":[{"text":"Respond to the situation rather than force a movement already begun.","fact_ids":["sec07-F29","sec07-F33","sec07-F34"]}],"narration":{"text":"Beginning a maneuver does not end the need to yield. The overtaking driver retains the duty toward the vehicle being passed even when it slows or stops. A driver also stays out of an intersection that cannot be cleared. Emergency vehicles with the described siren and lights require the stated move right, attention to loudspeaker directions and a stop until the vehicle passes. These are different examples of responding to the current situation. A desired route, a started pass or an earlier favorable signal is not proof that the remaining movement may be forced regardless of what develops.","fact_ids":["sec07-F29","sec07-F33","sec07-F34"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":40,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-slide-5","kind":"self_check","title":{"text":"Keep the sidewalk-crossing duty","fact_ids":["sec07-F25","sec07-F26","sec07-F29"]},"lines":[{"text":"Leaving private property does not remove the pedestrian yielding instruction.","fact_ids":["sec07-F25","sec07-F26","sec07-F29"]}],"narration":{"text":"A driver leaves a driveway and treats the sidewalk crossing as part of a private-property departure with no pedestrian duty. What is overlooked? The handbook says drivers crossing sidewalks or entering and leaving these locations yield to pedestrians. That crossing permission is not permission to drive along the sidewalk. The same habit of identifying the situation helps at nearby traffic movements: a left turn still yields to oncoming through traffic, and no vehicle should enter an intersection without space to clear. Start with the actual crossing and preserve its remaining duties.","fact_ids":["sec07-F25","sec07-F26","sec07-F29"]},"estimated_narration_seconds":37,"media_role":"none","media_absence_reason":"text_first_pilot"},{"slide_id":"sec07-u02-slide-6","kind":"close","title":{"text":"Retain the reason for the stop","fact_ids":["sec07-F32","sec07-F34","sec07-F35","sec07-R13"]},"lines":[{"text":"Different signals keep their different stopping or caution conditions.","fact_ids":["sec07-F32","sec07-F34","sec07-F35","sec07-R13"]}],"narration":{"text":"Keep the different stopping signals with their described response. The red-flashing school-bus provision calls for the stated stop from either direction until the lights end, while a slowing or yellow-flashing bus calls for careful slowing. Do not merge caution and stopping into one assumed response. Also retain pedestrian stops and the prohibition on passing the vehicle protecting the crossing.
